question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility buy official store 2026

replays.text:
**It could be a good back-seat movie screen, but it isn’t an electronic display or projector.** TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in projection surface and sunshade; you’ll need a compatible portable projector separately. It offers rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing, with screen panels listed at about 47 and 50 inches.

It’s best suited to the **2025–2026 Model Y refresh**. Aurzen says it can fit the overall dimensions of 2020–2024 Ys for sky-roof viewing, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window on those earlier models. Projection is for use **only while parked**. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

**Where to buy:** [Buy directly from Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y). The listed price is **$119.99**; Aurzen says it’s available in the U.S., with free delivery, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty.

**Bottom line:** A promising option if you have a portable projector and a newer Model Y, especially for parked movie nights. If you want a screen that works without a separate projector—or one primarily for passengers to use while driving—this isn’t that.
